I will report my true preference order because, under the standard applicant-proposing Deferred Acceptance mechanism (which is strategy-proof for applicants), truthfully ranking schools is a dominant strategy — misrepresenting preferences cannot give me a better outcome and can only hurt me.

Practical considerations that reinforce truth-telling here:
- I have top priority (rank 1) at y and at w, so I am relatively secure at those schools compared to other applicants. That makes listing y first safe since it is also my top choice.
- Many other applicants favor y, so y may be crowded, but my priority 1 at y gives me a strong chance there; if I do not get y, the mechanism will consider my next choices.
- I prefer z to w, so I list z above w even though I also have priority 1 at w; the DA mechanism will respect that true ordering and my high priority at w serves as a good backup.
- x is my least preferred and I have lower priority there (2), so it belongs last.

Therefore I will submit my sincere ranking: y > z > w > x.
